title: Bomb threat by phone
version: NZ Police 'Bomb threat checklist' card (POL 940, printed '11/02', i.e. November 2002 or 2011-02; no other date); NZ Police web pages 'Suspicious mail and bomb threats' and 'How you can help' (no dates shown, footer 2026); ANZCTC 'Improvised Explosive Device (IED) Guidelines for Crowded Places' (Commonwealth of Australia 2023, CC BY 4.0, Appendix B Telephoned bomb threat checklist); all read 20 Nov 2026
sourceNote: Direct download was refused (proxy blocks police.govt.nz, protectivesecurity.govt.nz and nationalsecurity.gov.au) and web search gave titles only, so every line was read by a fetch tool asked to quote exact lines (long sentences in pieces, rejoined). No PDF was in sources/. Sections: A NZ Police bomb threat checklist card (main source; A1 10 questions, A2 exact wording, A3 action: report to / phone number / trace 111 / police advised / date-time / member's name, A4 caller's voice, A5 threat language, A6 background noises and kind of call, A7 sex and age, A8 call taken, A9 recipient). B NZ Police web pages (B1 bomb threats: keep the checklist by the phone, employer decides whether to search or evacuate; B2 unattended bag: don't touch, ask who owns it, keep people away, call 111). C ANZCTC IED Guidelines for Crowded Places 2023 (joint Australia-NZ committee but an Australian publication that says dial 000; C1 Appendix B phone checklist: remain calm, talk to caller, note number, record call, exact wording, 11 questions, record time call ended, inform building security or coordinating manager, dial 000, then fill caller details, plus email/social media threats; C2 communicated threats: report to police, treat as credible until proven otherwise, 4 assessment questions, 3 response levels; C3 white level inspections by staff; C4 suspicious items: do not touch, tilt or tamper, no mobile phones or radios within 25 metres, evacuate at least 100 metres, at least 500 metres for a vehicle, no one in line of sight; C5 evacuation: incident/security manager decides, total or partial, factors, secondary devices at assembly points; C6 stand-off). Not captured: the chart linking the 4 assessment questions to the 3 response levels; some ANZCTC field labels (names/times of who was informed, signature block) and the exact words of the web-log period (7 days before to 48 hours after, from a summary only); ends of three long sentences (marked). No bomb threat guidance was found on protectivesecurity.govt.nz (searches returned none; site not reachable). Differences: (1) Question order: NZ Police starts 'When is the Bomb going to explode?' then 'Where is the Bomb?'; ANZCTC starts 'Where exactly is the bomb right now?' then 'When is it going to explode?'. NZ asks kind of bomb, what will make it explode, explosive type and quantity, where are you; ANZCTC asks what it contains, how detonated, did you place it or who did, telephone number, group or alone. (2) Emergency number: NZ 111 (and 'Trace 111' on the card); ANZCTC 000. (3) Who to tell: NZ card 'Report call immediately to' a blank to fill in locally, then Police; ANZCTC building security or coordinating manager, then police. (4) Voice, language and background lists differ (NZ free-text fields; ANZCTC tick boxes, e.g. ANZCTC has Foul, NZ has Abusive and Message read by caller; NZ has Aircraft and Vehicle; ANZCTC has PA System, Static, Booth, Crockery). (5) Only ANZCTC says remain calm, talk to the caller, note the displayed number and record the call; the NZ card has no during-call instructions. Gaps: neither source says 'do not hang up' or to keep the line open after the call, or to keep the caller talking beyond 'talk to the caller'; neither says how to decide to evacuate in plain rules: NZ Police leaves it to the employer and ANZCTC to the incident/security manager with police; no evacuation distance is given for a phone threat with no item found (100 m and 500 m apply to a found suspicious item, and are Australian guidance); NZ sources give no distance or radio/mobile phone rule; the NZ card date (11/02) is old and no newer NZ version was found; search procedure and assembly points are left to local plans.
status: Reviewer: 3 instructions missed and 14 findings, all fixed; 4 gaps the sources leave open. 116 of 116 quotes exact (web copy).
